For fixed \(\mu\), the selector endpoints are affine linear-program projections and shrinking positive margins alone do not violate Cho--Russell's compactness, bounded-envelope, feasibility, or fixed positive absolutely continuous perturbation requirements. Their theorem is therefore a transferred benchmark for that fixed-cost reduction. Joint estimation of \(\mu\) from cells with \(\pi_{n,cx}\geq\kappa_n\downarrow0\) is not directly covered because the inverse-cell representation need not have their uniformly bounded envelope.

For fixed \(\mu\), an epigraph formulation gives an affine projection, but Gafarov's uniform positive slack constant fails on the full shrinking-margin transport class: on a \(2\times2\) row of total mass \(\kappa_n\), the residual norm of two nonnegativity constraints is at most \(\kappa_n\), so the class slack tends to zero. His theorem also requires the stated rank, no-overidentification or dual-uniqueness, and moment conditions. Jointly estimated \(\mu\) is a transferred benchmark only on subclasses satisfying those conditions and uniform moments for the estimated coefficients.

open_obligations.what_is_open: On the explicitly defined response-interior subclass, prove or refute the proposed numerical-delta sufficiency window, establish or refute rare-margin face-switching sharpness, and compare excess width and rate requirements with the projected-region, Cho--Russell, and Gafarov procedures on subclasses where each method's hypotheses are jointly satisfied.
open_obligations.obstruction: The zero-coverage construction proves that absolute bounded-Lipschitz approximation is insufficient on the unrepaired class, but it has fixed margins and therefore says nothing about face switching. Response interiority removes that witness but does not itself establish uniform localization of nonunique primal and dual faces, relative multiplier accuracy, quantile anti-concentration, or a common rate expansion for the four procedures. Cho--Russell uses fixed positive random perturbations, while Gafarov requires uniform rank, slack, uniqueness, and moment constants that need not hold on the full shrinking-margin class.
open_obligations.attempted: The strengthened all-zero construction was derived with \(b_n=1/\log(n+1)\) and gives zero coverage under every schedule. A deterministic projected-region fallback was proved. The comparator LPs were then audited separately for fixed and jointly estimated costs. These steps isolate the remaining task but do not supply the new uniform face-localization or comparative-width theorem.

prose_updates.tldr: The causal selector envelope and its fixed-law directional inference remain established. The new uniform result is a sharp diagnostic: on one fixed-margin, fixed-cell singleton with response means \(2b_n/n\), both bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian approximations vanish while the paired multiplier numerical-delta envelope has coverage tending to zero for every deterministic step schedule. This is not an impossibility result, because projecting any honest simultaneous primitive region through \(L\) and \(U\) yields an honest fallback. Comparative width and shrinking-margin rates remain open on an explicitly response-interior subclass.

project_justification.gap: Available affine-LP methods do not settle the same joint rare-margin and estimated-cost problem under the present assumptions. For fixed \(\mu\), Cho--Russell remains a transferable randomly perturbed-LP benchmark even as margins shrink, whereas Gafarov's uniform positive slack condition fails on the full shrinking-margin transport class. When \(\mu\) is estimated from response cells whose probabilities may approach zero, neither transfer is automatic because inverse-cell influence envelopes or moments can diverge. The procedure-specific numerical-delta rate and width comparison therefore remains open after imposing response interiority.
project_justification.niche: The incremental contribution is a schedule-independent zero-coverage response-boundary diagnostic for the named paired numerical-delta implementation, together with an exact projected-region fallback. The next subfield question is comparative: on a common response-regular subclass, does row-feasible numerical delta buy narrower intervals or weaker margin-rate requirements than projection or transferred affine-LP methods? The conjectured \(n\kappa_n^3\) threshold is not an established frontier.
project_justification.fill: The note sets \(b_n=1/\log(n+1)\) after a finite-row adjustment, uses Bernoulli means \(2b_n/n\), and proves that the all-zero event tends to probability one, collapses the empirical-influence multiplier critical value to zero, and forces coverage to zero although both absolute bounded-Lipschitz discrepancies vanish. It also defines \(\mathrm{CI}_n^{\mathrm{proj}}=[\inf_{\widetilde\beta\in\mathcal R_n}L(\widetilde\beta),\sup_{\widetilde\beta\in\mathcal R_n}U(\widetilde\beta)]\) and proves the deterministic inclusion from primitive-region coverage. The remaining comparison is confined to \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa,\eta}^{\mathrm{int}}\).

sampling_model.design: For fixed-law supporting results, regular samples jointly identify \(p\), \(r\), and \(\mu\). For uniform questions, row \(n\) contains independent observations with fixed finite supports and cell-probability floors indexed by \(\kappa_n\). The zero-coverage diagnostic uses uniform \(2\times2\) response-study cells, fixed deployment margins, and Bernoulli means \(2b_n/n\), where \(b_n=1/\log(n+1)\) after finitely many rows.
sampling_model.units: Target contexts and actions are multinomial draws; separate interventional response units identify every finite \((c,x)\) cell. Dependence across stacked regular components is allowed through a declared row influence vector. In the singleton diagnostic the margins are observed without error and only the four response means are sampled.
sampling_model.treatment: The response study observes micro action \(X\); target macro action \(h\) uses an unknown context-only selector calibrated to \(r\). The response-boundary theorem changes only the sampling law and ridge for the identified micro-response means and does not alter the causal selector class or target interval.
sampling_model.overlap: The class \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) imposes floors on \(p_n\), \(r_n\), and \(\pi_n\), but no lower bound on Bernoulli response means. It therefore contains the zero-coverage singleton even though deployment and study-cell probabilities are fixed. The comparative open question uses the primitive subclass \(\eta\leq\mu_{n,cx}\leq1-\eta\); whether the proposed margin and numerical-step rates suffice there is not proved.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On the singleton, the stacked estimator and empirical-influence multiplier both converge to a degenerate Gaussian law in absolute bounded-Lipschitz distance. With probability tending to one all responses are zero, every ridged cost estimate equals \(b_n/n\), the multiplier critical value is zero, and the true cost equals \(2b_n/n\). For general use, a simultaneous primitive region \(\mathcal R_n\) can instead be projected through the endpoint maps to obtain a coverage-preserving fallback.

prose_updates.related_work: VanderWeele and Hernán motivate specifying version-assignment laws, and Béal and Latouche supply the PDX deployment setting. D'Haultfoeuille, Gaillac, and Maurel inform the unlinked-margin transport envelope; Rubenstein et al., Beckers and Halpern, and Xia and Bareinboim inform the structural abstraction semantics. The present free-selector class proves the Xia--Bareinboim Definition-6 identity selector by selector and explicitly does not preserve one fixed Equation-11 canonical Layer-3 map. For inference, Fang--Santos and Hong--Li support the fixed-law directional numerical-delta result, while the new theorem diagnoses a boundary failure of that specific implementation. The comparator inclusion audit is as follows. With fixed \(\mu\), each endpoint is an affine transportation-LP projection. Shrinking positive margins alone do not violate Cho--Russell's compact-polyhedron, bounded-envelope, feasibility, i.i.d., or fixed positive absolutely continuous perturbation requirements, so their randomly perturbed LP is a transferred fixed-cost benchmark; it covers the identified set conservatively and attains exact coverage on an outer perturbed set, not the same interval target. Their published theorem does not directly verify the jointly estimated-\(\mu\) rare-cell design, because representing a conditional cell mean in the objective uses inverse cell probabilities and the required common bounded envelope can fail as \(\pi_{n,cx}\downarrow0\). Gafarov's affine epigraph formulation is another fixed-cost benchmark and permits flat primal faces, but his uniform class requires positive rank and slack constants and, in the stated main case, no overidentification and unique dual solutions. On a \(2\times2\) transport row of mass \(\kappa_n\), two nonnegativity residuals have norm at most \(\kappa_n\), so the required uniform slack constant fails as \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\); nonunique dual faces create a separate exclusion. Jointly estimated \(\mu\) is covered by that framework only after verifying its affine coefficient representation and uniform \(2+\epsilon\) moment bounds, which the present floor \(\pi_{n,cx}\geq\kappa_n\downarrow0\) does not supply. These are transferred benchmarks on their admissible subclasses, not results established for the full class here. The projected-region fallback is assumption-transparent and uniformly honest whenever its primitive region is, but no comparative width theorem is claimed.
prose_updates.interpretation: For a fixed interior deployment law, the paired numerical-delta method remains pointwise valid even with nonunique transport faces. Uniform use near a response boundary is different: absolute Gaussian accuracy can coexist with a nearly certain all-zero sample, a zero critical value, and zero coverage. Practitioners should either verify a response-interior or equally strong variance diagnostic before using that numerical-delta envelope, or use the projected-region fallback. For the Béal--Latouche PDX application, superiority to control should be reported as uniform only when the lower selector endpoint exceeds the control benchmark and the uncertainty method covers that lower endpoint; the new diagnostic warns that rare positive outcomes can invalidate the numerical-delta certificate even when allocation margins are well behaved.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper proves a schedule-independent zero-coverage theorem for one collapsing-response singleton and the specific paired multiplier numerical-delta envelope. It also proves an exact deterministic projection fallback from any simultaneous primitive confidence region. It does not prove a minimax impossibility for other methods, a sufficient or sharp \(n\kappa_n^3\) threshold, or a width advantage over projected-region, Cho--Russell, or Gafarov procedures. Cho--Russell transfers cleanly only to the audited fixed-cost LP subclass unless additional estimated-cost envelope conditions are verified; Gafarov additionally requires uniform rank, slack, uniqueness, and moment conditions that exclude parts of the shrinking-margin and nonunique-dual class. The remaining comparison is open on \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa,\eta}^{\mathrm{int}}\). The structural SCM realization, sharp selector interval, endpoint certificates, fixed-map obstruction, cycle criterion, fixed-interior derivative, and pointwise numerical-delta result retain their supporting scope.
